purpose: Make K-line analysis explicit, quantitative and session-aware without turning visual candlestick names into unvalidated directional alpha.
principle: K-line information is important as a compressed representation of auction/path state, but named candlestick patterns are not trusted by themselves. Use normalized structure, location, volume, acceptance/rejection, session and multi-timeframe context.

mandatory_checks: prior and developing POC when volume-at-price is available
VAH/VAL when a rights-clean volume-at-price profile is available
HVN/LVN and thin/accepted price zones when available
false break / rejection back into prior value or box
box migration after sustained acceptance outside the prior range

operational_definitions.touch: Price reaches a reference level without sufficient evidence of persistence beyond it.
operational_definitions.break: Price trades beyond a reference level; a break alone is not acceptance.
operational_definitions.acceptance: Persistence beyond a reference level supported by time/closed bars and, when available, volume/participation. Exact thresholds must be preregistered per data frequency rather than chosen after the fact.
operational_definitions.rejection: Price trades beyond a reference level but returns into the prior value/box without sustained acceptance.
operational_definitions.box_migration: A prior balance area is replaced by a new accepted range after sustained trade outside the old box.

modules.data_boundary: True volume profile requires actual volume-at-price/tick information. OHLC-derived profile is a proxy and must be labeled PROXY_PROFILE.

mandatory_checks: opening-range width normalized by recent intraday volatility/ATR
relationship to prior day high/low, overnight high/low, VWAP and value area
modules.research_boundary: External index-futures research supports opening-range information, but JNU-specific directional promotion requires preregistered OSE OOS/forward validation.

mandatory_checks: range normalized by ATR or session realized volatility
volume normalized by time-of-day baseline when available
alignment or conflict between lower and higher timeframe structure
modules.rule: Do not treat named candlestick labels as directional alpha. Describe the bar numerically and condition it on location/regime.

mandatory_checks: upside versus downside realized semivariance when intraday data permit
large signed intraday jumps relative to local volatility
interaction with Nikkei 225 VI and HAR-RSV state
modules.rationale: Signed realized variation and jump sign can contain incremental information for future volatility; use for risk/confidence and stop/target scaling, not a direct direction vote.

prohibited_shortcuts: Do not assign a bullish/bearish vote solely because a candle is called doji, hammer, engulfing, morning star or similar.
Do not compute POC/VAH/VAL from invented volume-at-price data.
Do not call a one-tick excursion a breakout.
Do not call a breakout accepted without persistence evidence.
Do not tune acceptance/bar thresholds after seeing outcome data.
output_requirements: State whether price is touching, breaking, accepting or rejecting key structure.
State opening-range/initial-balance condition when intraday data are available.
State whether K-line observations are exact-volume/tick based or OHLC/proxy based.
research_sources: Blume, Easley & O'Hara (1994), Journal of Finance: volume contains information not in price alone.
Holmberg, Lönnbark & Lundström (2013), Finance Research Letters: opening-range breakout evidence in futures.
Tsai et al. (2019), IEEE Access: opening/closing underlying-market periods concentrate volume/return fluctuations across index futures.
Patton & Sheppard (2015), Review of Economics and Statistics: signed realized semivariance/jumps improve volatility forecasts.
Candlestick evidence is mixed; recent out-of-sample studies do not support treating named candlestick patterns as stable standalone alpha.
